text: Italy's unemployment rate fell from 11.9% in 2015 to 7.7% in 2023.
why: Regression: a whole year on a monthly series was read as one month (2015-01, 2023-12).

claims.quote: Italy's unemployment rate fell from 11.9% in 2015 to 7.7% in 2023
claims.justification: Yearly averages of the monthly series: 12.02 (2015) and 7.68 (2023), within 0.5 points of 11.9 and 7.7; the rate fell.

text: In 2011 Italy's youth unemployment was 29%; today it is 43.3%.
why: Regression: the monthly youth series was turned down for being monthly, and 'today it is 43.3%' lost its value.

claims.justification: The 2011 average of the monthly youth rate is 29.19, within 0.5 points of 29.
No date is given, so 'today' is the latest month: 19.9 in 2026-09 (Eurostat, updated 2026-11-05), far from 43.3.

text: Renzi, 2018: Since I took office, youth unemployment has fallen 12 points, from 44% to 32%.
why: Regression: 'latest' in a 2018 statement was read as 2026-09.

claims.justification: Said in 2018: latest is 2018-11 (32.0). From 2014-02 (42.7) that is a fall of 10.7 points, not 12 (± 0.5).

text: Letta, 2013: Italy's youth unemployment has reached 37% and has been rising for years.
why: Regression: 'rising for years' was fitted from 1983.

claims.justification: The 5 years before the claim date: yearly averages 21.4 (2008) to 40.1 (2013), rising every year.

text: Grillo: At the end of 2013 Italy's debt-to-GDP ratio hit 132.6%, up from 127% in 2012.
why: Regression: a level claim's plan answered with value_at and change and was rejected twice.

text: Renzi, 2013: Italy's public debt is 133% of GDP.

claims.quote: Italy's public debt is 133% of GDP
claims.justification: 132.0 in 2013, within 133 ± 1.83 (half a unit plus 1%, D020).

text: Renzi, December 2015: Italy's greenhouse gas emissions are down 23% compared with 1990.
why: Regression: compared with 2024 instead of what was published by December 2015.

claims.quote: Italy's greenhouse gas emissions are down 23% compared with 1990
claims.justification: By 2015-12 inventories ran to 2013 (18-month lag): 520.6 to 450.5 Mt, down 13.5%, not 23%.

text: EPA, 2017: US per capita carbon dioxide emissions fell more than 18% between 2000 and 2014.
why: Regression: 'more than 18%' was checked as exactly 18%.

claims.quote: US per capita carbon dioxide emissions fell more than 18% between 2000 and 2014
claims.justification: 21.40 to 17.12 t per person: down 20.0%, more than 18%.

text: Facebook post, 2013: Unemployment in South Africa has increased by 60% in the past 19 years.
why: Regression: the 19-year lookback ran to 2025 instead of the claim date.

claims.quote: Unemployment in South Africa has increased by 60% in the past 19 years
claims.justification: Said in 2013: latest year out is 2012. The rate went from 23.07 (1994) to 24.73: up 7.2%, not 60%. (The claim may mean the number of unemployed, which the catalog does not have.)
